title: A Landfall for the Rivergate
premise: Gideon Galloway has spent a decade keeping her floatplane and her past small, ferrying medicine into the Rivergate interior where the glacier route opens only weeks each year. When her old rival Maren Kessler hires her crew to run the flooded lower river during monsoon season, Gideon realizes the job is a cover for recovering something she swore off long ago: the wreck of her father's plane, and the truth about the crash that made her an exile. Betrayed by a crew member selling their position to Kessler, Gideon must navigate the dying river with a leaking boat and the help of Tomas, a stranger with his own debts to the water. In the end she reaches the wreck, learns her father chose to hide the cargo rather than let it be used, and chooses truth over invisibility—flying out through the calving glacier's last open window with evidence that will cost her everything but finally give her somewhere to belong.
about_author: Paloma Vasquez is a former river guide who spent six seasons in remote northern bush country before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people whose loyalties are tested by landscapes that do not care whether they survive.

chapters.title: Weather Coming Down
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She lands at Rivergate with medicine and gossip, sensing the monsoon building behind the ridgelines. A telegram from Maren Kessler waits, offering money for a run downriver no one else will fly. The beat: dread disguised as routine, as Gideon recognizes the job is bait aimed squarely at her.

chapters.title: The Sworn-Off Water
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, with a flashback to the night her father's plane went into the lower river fifteen years ago. She refuses Kessler's offer; Kessler reveals she knows where the wreck lies and that the ice window closes in three weeks. The beat: the past tightening its grip, forcing Gideon to weigh silence against answers.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. He signs on as deckhand for wages he desperately needs, reading the crew: loyal old mechanic Ruiz, sharp-eyed deckhand Priya, and quiet Gideon. He notices someone photographing the cargo manifest. The beat: uneasy belonging, as Tomas senses the job is not what it seems.

chapters.title: Downstream of Every Rule
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The boat runs the swollen river past drowned villages; a near-capsize costs them fuel and nearly Priya. Gideon begins to suspect a leak in the crew when supplies are disturbed. The beat: survival bonding under pressure, shadowed by the first real crack of mistrust.

chapters.title: What the Manifest Said
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She discovers pages torn from the manifest naming medical crates that were never medicine—and realizes Kessler's client wants what Gideon's father hid. Torn between loyalty to the crew and a payout that could free her family, she photographs the pages. The beat: temptation, and the birth of the betrayal.

chapters.title: Monsoon Hold
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Stormbound on a gravel bar, the crew shares stories by lamplight; Gideon almost tells Tomas the truth about her father but stops herself. That night a satellite phone call goes out from the treeline. The beat: intimacy deepening even as the traitor moves, dramatic irony tightening the screws.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. With the hull seeping and the glacier window opening early, they must run the gorge or lose the season. Mid-rapid, Kessler's rival salvage team appears upstream—they were tipped off. Gideon realizes the leak was never just in the boat. The beat: betrayal revealed, trust shattered, stakes doubled.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Confluence
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Caught between crews, Priya confesses to Gideon and offers what she stole back; Ruiz takes a beating shielding her from Kessler's men. They escape down a side channel only Tomas knows. The beat: guilt, forgiveness half-granted, and the fragile re-forging of loyalty around shared truth.

chapters.title: Calving
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. At the wreck site beneath the glacier face, they raise the crate while the ice groans and calves around them. Inside: her father's logbook proving he scuttled the contraband rather than deliver it—and naming Kessler's family as the buyers. The beat: catharsis and terror fused, as the truth surfaces literally with the ice.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, closing with Tomas's. Flying the last open window over the calving glacier, logbook aboard, Gideon chooses to land at Rivergate and tell the whole valley the truth instead of vanishing again. Kessler's claim collapses; the community that once exiled her offers her a hangar, a place. The beat: belonging earned through honesty—the price paid, the landing made.
